slides.title: Exponential Map
text: Exponential map: Takes a tangent vector 𝜈 ∈ 𝑇1 ℳ and transports it along the unique
geodesic which satisfies 𝛾 0 = 𝑝 and 𝛾̇ 0 = 𝜈 to the point exp1 𝜈 = 𝛾(1).
Output of the exponential map is a point on ℳ.
Conceptually like “addition” in a Euclidean space,
case in point exp1 𝜈 = 𝑝 + 𝑣, ∀𝑝 ∈ ℝ6 .

slides.title: Logarithmic Map
text: Logarithmic map: log 1 : ℳ → 𝑇1 ℳ. Takes a point on ℳ back
to the tangent space of a base point by following 𝛾.
Output of a logarithmic map is 𝜈 ∈ 𝑇1 ℳ
Usually, inverse of the exponential map.
The log map is well-defined only in a neighbourhood
of 𝑝 where exp1 is a diffeomorphism.
